newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Perwaja back with new FRN.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Perwaja back with new FRN.

text.p: Malaysia's Perwaja Terengganu Sdn Bhd returned with its re-priced floating-rate note (FRN) through Standard Chartered Bank, bankers said on Friday.
The five-year issue, guaranteed by the Malaysian government, is still for US$400 million but carries a coupon of just 15 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
Fees are 15 basis points for participants committing US$10 million, for an all-in yield of 18 basis points.
This is lower than last week's all-in of 23 basis points, but bankers noted the government guarantee lifts it to effectively sovereign risk.
One banker close to the deal expected the issue to go well despite the lower pricing, but some bankers had reservations.
A Japanese banker said about 22 basis points would have been fairer and the issue size was too large.
Other recent deals from Malaysian borrowers have paid substantially more for shorter periods, although they lacked government guarantees.
Public Bank featured an all-in of 32 basis points on its HK$1.2 billion floating-rate certificate of deposit (FRCD) issue.
Arab Malaysian Merchant Banking Bhd is paying an all-in of 29.5 basis points over three years in its US$100 million.
But the government guarantee adds lustre to Perwaja Terengganu, and Malaysian paper is generally looking more attractive compared to some Thai paper.
In other news, Hong Kong's Airport Authority is still talking to banks about a three-year loan for a second runway, and price talk is "in the 20's" according to bankers.
However, it is keeping its options open.
The authority has not yet drawn down last year's HK$8.2 billion loan and is working on a HK$5 billion note-debt facility to be operated by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.
Also expected in the market are Ng Fung Hong Ltd with a US$150 million loan, and Guangdong Enterprises.
Yet another Hong Kong dollar floating-rate certificate of deposit (FRCD) issue was launched in the territory's increasingly crowded Hong Kong dollar FRCD market.

Bank of America (Asia) launched its HK$1.5 billion FRCD hard on the heels of an FRCD from Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, paying an all-in yield of 30 basis points, against Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi's 25 basis point all-in this week.
But Bank of America (Asia) would carry a 100-percent weighting, against only 20 percent for Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi.
"That's worth a couple of points. I don't know whether it's worth five basis points," one syndicate manager said.
"Bank of Tokyo is fairly priced. It may be that Bank of America is generously priced," another said.
About HK$15 billion of Hong Kong dollar FRCDs have been issued in Hong Kong since the beginning of June in a massive wave of banks arming themselves to on-lend to corporates.
-- Sean Kennedy newsroom (852) 2847 4043
